test_title: PYST 7: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence.

He said that she had been trying to reach him for several days.

options.text: He said, "She has been trying to reach me for several days."
He said, "She had been trying to reach me for several days."
He said, "She was trying to reach me for several days."
He said, "She is trying to reach me for several days."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that she had been trying to reach him for several days.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"she had been trying" becomes "She has been trying"**
 
 
• The **Past Perfect Continuous** tense ("had been trying") in indirect speech typically converts back to the **Present Perfect Continuous** ("has been trying") in direct speech.
 
• The duration "for several days" strongly indicates the use of a perfect continuous tense.
 
 
 
• **"reach him" becomes "reach me"**
 
 
• The pronoun **"him"** (referring to the subject 'He') must change to the first-person **"me"** to reflect the speaker's own words in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains "said," followed by a comma and opening quotation marks.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks: **"She has been trying to reach me for several days."**
 
• The sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a period inside the closing quotation mark.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *He said, "She has been trying to reach me for several days."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He said, 'She had been trying to reach me for several days.'" 

 
 
• Uses **Past Perfect Continuous**. While grammatically possible, in transformation exercises, we backshift tenses. Keeping "had been" doesn't reflect the standard conversion from indirect back to direct.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said, 'She was trying to reach me for several days.'" 
 
 
• Uses **Past Continuous**. While Past Continuous can change to Past Perfect Continuous, the "for several days" timeframe usually requires a Perfect tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said, 'She is trying to reach me for several days.'" 
 
 
• Uses **Present Continuous**. This would shift to Past Continuous ("was trying") in indirect speech, and it is grammatically incorrect to use "is trying" with a "for..." duration.
